page: The Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is an x86_64 cloud compute instance categorized within the memory-optimized tier of the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core at 2.0 GHz, supporting two hardware threads per core. System memory is sized at 16.0 GB RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage includes a bundled 120 GB local NVMe SSD, and each instance receives one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server includes no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluation reveals asymmetric performance dictated by single-core capabilities and core count limitations. Single-threaded instruction pipelines perform competently, reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 3013.38 (top 25%), rapid single-threaded gzip compression at 32.61 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 14.3 GB/sec. Modern instruction vector sets are supported, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic hardware extensions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). In contrast, total multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU hardware ceiling, yielding weak aggregate rankings across the PassMark CPU score (4034.68), Geekbench multi-core (2278.0), and Clang software compilation benchmarks.

Memory subsystem benchmarks reflect standard shared virtualization throughput, with 172.73 GB/sec cached small-block reads, dropping to 26.94 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 24.91 GB/sec on writes. Storage and operational tests yielded 3.12 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 5.94 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Machine learning execution matches the physical boundaries of a two-thread processor, managing 126.57 tokens per second for small 135M model text generation, but dropping to a poor 5.37 tokens per second on 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-m-2c-16g-120s offers an economical entry point for memory-heavy services that do not require extensive parallel compute. Workloads with low CPU concurrency demands, such as light in-memory caching, memory-intensive backend tasks, staging environments, intermediate ETL queues, and moderate web services, align well with its specification profile.
description: The Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance featuring an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core at 2.0 GHz) and 16.0 GB of RAM. The server includes 120 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 1 public IPv4 address, operating without a discrete GPU. Benchmarks reflect robust single-core compute performance, highlighted by strong stress-ng single-core (3013.38) and fast single-thread gzip compression (32.61 GB/sec). However, multi-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth fall into lower percentile tiers due to the dual-thread ceiling. With an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation, this instance provides cost-effective density for memory-sensitive, low-concurrency applications, including lightweight Redis instances, staging databases, background ETL processing, and low-traffic web applications.
